sourceArticle.title: Definity embeds agents inside Spark pipelines to catch failures before they reach agentic AI systems
sourceArticle.author: Sean Michael Kerner

athenaOutput.directive: Architect and implement a fully autonomous, declarative agentic framework for pre-emptive failure detection and self-remediation within all Creative Liberation Engine data pipelines, ensuring zero human wait time and empowering domain experts.
athenaOutput.rationale: The Definity article highlights a critical need to embed agents directly within data pipelines to catch failures before they impact downstream agentic AI systems. Our constitutional laws and prior strategic decisions (e.g., '4 YAML Files Instead of PySpark' and 'Zero human wait time') mandate a self-hosted, complete, and fully autonomous solution that empowers all Creative Liberation Engine stakeholders, including analysts, to define robust, self-healing data flows. This directive aims to create a foundational capability for resilient, self-managing AI operations.

options.title: Declarative In-Pipeline Guardian Agents
options.description: Develop a self-hosted, declarative framework (e.g., YAML/DSL-based) that enables Creative Liberation Engine stakeholders, including analysts, to define and deploy 'guardian agents' directly within data pipelines. These agents will autonomously monitor data quality, pipeline health, and predefined failure conditions, executing immediate, self-healing remediation actions to prevent issues from propagating to downstream agentic AI systems, all without human intervention.
options.tradeoffs: High initial development cost for the framework; complexity in balancing powerful agentic logic with a simple, declarative interface for non-developers; potential for configuration errors if validation is not robust. However, it strongly aligns with Creative Liberation Engine's constitutional principles of sovereignty, quality, completeness, and zero human wait time, while empowering diverse users.

options.title: Micro-Agent Swarms for Real-time Anomaly Detection
options.description: Deploy small, specialized 'micro-agents' at each critical node or stage of a Spark-like pipeline. These agents would continuously analyze data streams for anomalies, deviations, or specific error patterns using lightweight ML models, signaling upstream agents for remediation or triggering pre-defined automated responses.
options.tradeoffs: Potentially high computational overhead if not meticulously optimized for distributed environments; complex orchestration and lifecycle management for a large number of distributed micro-agents; provides very high responsiveness and granular monitoring.

options.title: Predictive Failure Agents with Historical Learning
options.description: Implement agents that learn from historical pipeline failures and successes, along with associated data characteristics and environmental factors. These agents would use predictive analytics to anticipate potential failures before they occur, triggering pre-emptive adjustments, resource scaling, or warnings based on learned patterns.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant volumes of high-quality historical data for effective training; initial training period for agents to become effective; potential for false positives/negatives in predictions; highly proactive but might miss novel failure modes.

options.title: Centralized Agentic Control Plane with Distributed Probes
options.description: Establish a central 'Creative Liberation Engine Control Plane' that orchestrates and monitors distributed 'probes' (lightweight agents) embedded within various data pipelines. The control plane would aggregate signals, apply global policies, and dispatch specialized remediation agents as needed, acting as the brain for the entire pipeline monitoring ecosystem.
options.tradeoffs: Architectural complexity due to the distributed nature of probes and centralized control; potential for a single point of failure if the control plane is not designed with extreme resilience; strong central governance and consistent policy enforcement.

options.title: Agent-driven Self-Healing Pipeline Components
options.description: Design future Creative Liberation Engine data pipeline components to be inherently 'agentic,' meaning each component contains embedded logic to detect and self-correct common failures (e.g., automatic retries, data cleansing, schema adaptation, error isolation) without external intervention from a separate monitoring agent.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant re-architecture and development effort for every pipeline component; difficult to implement comprehensively across all possible failure modes; highly resilient at the component level but might lack system-wide oversight; a long-term vision.

options.title: Hybrid Human-in-the-Loop Agent Orchestration
options.description: Agents primarily focus on detection and flagging potential issues, presenting comprehensive diagnostics and suggested remediations to human operators for review, approval, or manual intervention. Agents would learn from human decisions to improve future recommendations.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates Article XX (Zero human wait time) by introducing a human bottleneck; while it could build trust and improve learning initially, it fundamentally impedes the goal of full autonomy and immediate remediation.
